faq.q: How much does it cost to get licensed in California after the bar?
faq.a: Plan on $900 to $1,498: the $900 general applicant moral character fee plus a first license fee of $0, $299, or $598, depending on your admission month (Rule 2.12).

faq.q: Is it cheaper to get sworn in to the California bar in December?
faq.a: Yes. Under Rule 2.12, admission between June 1 and November 30 means a $299 half-year fee. Admission in December carries no first license fee for that year. Either way the full $598 annual fee is due March 30.

faq.q: Can a notary swear me in to the California bar?
faq.a: Yes. A notary public can administer the attorney's oath, but California notaries can only do it in person, not virtually. Print your DocuSign form so the notary can sign and seal it.

faq.q: How long is a passing California bar score valid?
faq.a: Five years from the last day of the exam you passed (Rule 4.17). You must take the oath and register within that window.

faq.q: Does California have a first-year CLE requirement?
faq.a: Yes. New attorneys must finish the State Bar's 10-hour New Attorney Training by the last day of the month of their one-year anniversary.

faq.q: Can I transfer a UBE score to California?
faq.a: No. California does not accept transferred UBE or MBE scores.

points: Bring a UBE score of 266 or higher.

faq.q: How much does it cost to get admitted in New York after the bar?
faq.a: The required post-bar fee is the $375 attorney registration, paid before you take the oath. Transferring a UBE score from another state adds a $250 application fee and a $25 NCBE transcript fee.

faq.q: How many CLE credits do newly admitted New York attorneys need?
faq.a: 32 transitional credits over the first two years, 16 each year: 7 practice management or practice areas, 6 skills, and 3 ethics and professionalism.

faq.q: Can I transfer a UBE score to New York?
faq.a: Yes. New York accepts a UBE score of 266 or higher for three years from the exam date. You must also complete the NYLC and pass the NYLE.

faq.q: Do I need pro bono hours to be admitted in New York?
faq.a: Yes. Applicants admitted by exam must complete 50 hours of qualifying pro bono work before applying for admission.
